cases.migration_note: v2 returns a structured errors array with a specific code and parameter; the public OQ route wraps the error in an error object with a code integer and message string; no parameter field is returned.

cases.migration_note: Both v2 page_size and the public pageSize accept 1 to 99; the public default is 10; v2 page_size values in that range carry over unchanged. A malformed cursor returns an observed HTTP 500 on the public route.

cases.migration_note: v2 list does not validate id format in filter[]; a non-hex value returns no rows rather than a 400; do not rely on a filter validation error to detect malformed identifiers on the list route.
cases.public_oq: behavior not documented; a non-hex value in a filter likely returns an empty data array with HTTP 200; do not rely on a 400 for non-hex filter values
cases.v2: no error; list filter validation rejects only syntax errors and invalid enum values; non-hex id values in filter[] are not validated for id format and the query returns an empty data array with HTTP 200

cases.migration_note: v2 signals authorization failures with type unauthorized and retryable=false; the public OQ route returns a plain message string in the body on 400 or 401 with no explicit retry signal; do not use the v2 retryable flag as the retry signal on the public route.

cases.v2: 401 type unauthorized (empty errors array); retryable false; v2 maps HTTP 401 to type unauthorized only on the Object Query path

cases.migration_note: v2 returns retryable false in the response body for Object Query 500s; do not use the body retryable flag as a retry signal on the public route; implement retry logic based on the HTTP status code alone; a 429 is not documented but may occur and should be retried.
cases.public_oq: HTTP 500 not documented; an invalid cursor returns HTTP 500 with body {"errors":[{"message": string}]} (observed); a 429 response is not documented; retry on 429 and 5xx as you do today
cases.v2: 500, type internal_server_error, retryable false; upstream Object Query failures are returned as internal_server_error with retryable false

route.body: 400 and 404 errors return {"error":{"code": integer, "message": string}}; a missing bearer token returns HTTP 400 {"message":"No bearer token"}; an invalid bearer token returns HTTP 401 {"message":"Authentication error"}; an invalid cursor returns HTTP 500 {"errors":[{"message": string}]} (status codes observed on a test tenant; not all codes are in the contract)

For each row of `data[]` in the successful JSON response, build the `custom_fields` object. Always build the object: it is `{}` when the row has no custom fields. Use the `customFields` array when the row has one, otherwise the `custom_fields` array; turn each `{key, value, type}` entry into `key: value` (when a key appears more than once, the last entry wins). Then convert `long` and `number` values to numbers, convert `boolean` values to true or false, and leave other types unchanged; null values stay null. If the row has neither array, collect every property whose name ends in `__c` into the object; an empty array gives `{}` and the `__c` properties are then not used. Include `custom_fields` only when it was requested.

unsupported.note: The public APIs do not accept this header. The v2 API accepted the x-custom-auth and zuora-cache-enabled request headers; neither header has a public equivalent. The account list route did not wire a cache handler, so zuora-cache-enabled had no effect on this operation. The public APIs authenticate via a bearer token in the Authorization header and optionally accept zuora-entity-ids to scope the request to an entity and zuora-track-id for request tracing. Send the OAuth bearer token in the Authorization header. Pass zuora-entity-ids to scope the request to a specific entity, or zuora-track-id for request tracing. Do not send zuora-cache-enabled; the public APIs have no such header. No vetted GraphQL example is available.
